_about: THE ONE PLACE kit says what it ships, and where a service puts it.
Read by tests/staleness.py (--scope templates) and by the
parity-allowlist check in tests/validate.sh. Two consumers, one file:
AGENTS.md's rule is that a property stated in two places is a property
stated in zero times, and the artefact table is exactly the kind of
thing that drifts the moment it is written down twice.
A FIELD IS LOAD-BEARING
id       the name the reporter prints, and the name an allowlist entry
uses. It is a key, not a label: renaming one invalidates every
entry that named it, which is the correct outcome.
source   the path inside the kit checkout. `{lang}` interpolates the
service's DECLARED language (see `languageFrom`).
dest     the path inside the service repo, relative to its root.
bundle   a list of (source, dest) pairs instead of one each. The LGTM
stack is one artefact. docker-compose.yml binds FIVE paths, one
of which is the whole grafana/provisioning directory, so ten of
the eleven non-compose members are reachable from it and the
twelfth (.env.example) is `cp`'d to .env. Grading the members
separately would report a half-copied stack as a row of
successes and a row of absences, which is the thing this
grouping exists to prevent. It is deliberately NOT justified by
claiming a partial stack cannot start: checked against the real
fleet, no service compose file mounts any kit stack file at all,
so the seven that hold a compose file are replacements, and
`docker compose config` is green on five of the six. A partial
copy is a real state, but in THIS fleet it does not occur, and
the rationale must not rest on a claim the fleet contradicts.
languages which declared languages this artefact applies to. Absent
means every service, including one that has declared no
language at all — an undeclared service still has a
`mise.toml` question to answer.
needsLanguage true when the source path itself is `{lang}`-
interpolated, so the service must DECLARE a language before
the question can be asked at all. It is written out rather
than inferred from the presence of `{lang}` in `source`
because a wrong inference here is the fail-open direction:
the reporter would resolve `{lang}` to a guess and report
the guess as a measurement.
optional true when kit genuinely does not expect universal adoption.
Such an artefact is reported but does not, by itself, make a
service look broken.

artefacts._about_dest: kit's README documents `docker/Dockerfile`, and six of the nine services put theirs at the repository root instead. `destAlternatives` records that rather than leaving it to a human to notice: a path a service legitimately uses is not an absence, and grading a documented, working placement as `absent` is the same class of error as grading a drifted copy as `current` — a report that cries wolf is a report that is muted. The FIRST destination that exists wins, so this never guesses: it is a declared list of paths, resolved by existence, and `absent` still means absent of all of them.

artefacts._about_call: The ONE artefact a service does not copy. It calls the workflow, so a fix in kit reaches every service on the next run with no per-repo PR. `dest: @call` is what tells the reporter to check for a `uses: cafaye/kit/...@<ref>` line rather than for a file — and the check is that the line names the path the file is ACTUALLY at, because GitHub documents that subdirectories of .github/workflows are not supported and a `uses:` line pointing one resolves to nothing at run time.

artefacts._about_bundle: The local stack. It travels as twelve files because docker-compose.yml binds five of them by path and `cp`s the sixth, so the members are graded as ONE artefact: eleven separately-pinned cells would report a half-copied stack as a row of successes and a row of absences. Graded one way, a service holding eight of them reads as ONE cell with a breakdown. Not justified by claiming a partial stack cannot start — no service in the real fleet mounts any kit stack file, so the seven holding a compose file are replacements, and five of the six parse green.

artefacts._about_contract: THE CONNECTION CONTRACT, and the second half of kit's data topology. The `compose` bundle above is the CLUSTER — shared, identical for every service, fetched rather than copied — and these are what a service OWNS: the per-language config carrying `application_name`, `statement_timeout`, `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` and a bounded pool, and carrying NO pooler workaround, because kit runs no pooler (DECISIONS.md MD21).
artefacts._about_one_per_language: One artefact per language, with a LITERAL source rather than a `{lang}` template, and that is a deliberate shape rather than an inconsistency. `{lang}` interpolation cannot express these: the filename carries the language's own extension (`database.go.snippet`, `repo.exs.snippet`) and the destination differs per language too (`internal/db/db.go`, `lib/courier/database.ex`). Inventing a `perLanguage` field for it would be a change to what `tests/staleness.py` models, and this repository's rule is that a shape the reporter does not model is a decision that must be made deliberately and in the same commit — a reporter change, not an artefact-table change. So this uses the idiom both consumers already understand: a literal `source` with a `languages` filter. Six rows rather than one, and a service holding five of six is reported as five successes and one absence, which is the useful answer.
artefacts._about_optional: kit does not expect universal adoption in one commit: a service adopts its own language's snippet when it migrates onto the cluster. Reported either way — `absent` is a finding, not a failure.

artefacts._about_node: `node` and `bun` are ONE artefact with two languages, and deliberately so: bun runs node-postgres, so the snippet is byte-identical and a second file would be two things to keep in step for no difference in behaviour. `templates/database/contract.json` records the same fact as `alsoFor`, and a reader who wonders why there is no bun directory finds the answer in the node row's `languages` list.

artefacts._about: The machine-readable requirements kit's gate checks the six snippets against. Optional for a service — `templates/database/README.md` is what a human reads, and this is what a program reads — but shipped, because a service that wants to check ITS config against the contract needs the file rather than a prose list it would have to keep in step.
